input.question: Does every complete intersection have the Weak Lefschetz Property, meaning that multiplication by a general linear form has maximal rank in the case d = 1?

original_question: Does every complete intersection have the Weak Lefschetz Property, meaning that multiplication by a general linear form has maximal rank in the case d = 1?

original_paper.title: Pure O-Sequences: Known Results, Applications and Open Problems

rewritten_question: Let A = K[x1, ..., xr]/I be an Artinian complete intersection over a field of characteristic 0, where I is generated by a regular sequence of homogeneous polynomials, and let L be a general linear form. Must the multiplication map ×L: A_i → A_{i+1} have maximal rank for every degree i? Equivalently, does every Artinian complete intersection have the Weak Lefschetz Property?

resolution.status_reason: The primary paper explicitly says that, beyond codimension at most 3, it was not known whether all complete intersections have the WLP. Later papers used in the bounded search still describe the height-4 equigenerated case as a conjecture and report only partial progress, so the broader question does not appear resolved in the searched literature.

paper_evidence.quote: When I is an arbitrary artinian homogeneous ideal, the above maximal rank property for all d and i is called the Strong Lefschetz Property (SLP), and the case d = 1 is called the Weak Lefschetz Property (WLP).
It is not known (except in codimension ≤ 3, as noted below) whether all complete intersections have this property
It was used in [30] to show that any complete intersection I in K[x, y, z] over a field of characteristic zero has the WLP.
it has been conjectured that if char(k) = 0 then any complete intersection k-algebra, i.e. an algebra as above with I generated by a regular sequence, has the WLP.
We prove that the Weak Lefschetz Property for holds for any c.i. algebra A as above with d = 2 and m ≤ 4.
We consider the conjecture that all artinian height 4 complete intersections of forms of the same degree d have the Weak Lefschetz Property (WLP).
Our main results are (i) a proof that the property holds for d = 3, 4 and 5; (ii) a partial result showing maximal rank in a non-trivial but incomplete range
Based on this conjecture we outline an approach to proving WLP for all equigenerated complete intersections in four variables.
